source.title: Line of Sight: On Linear Representations in VLLMs
source.authors: Achyuta Rajaram; Sarah Schwettmann; Jacob Andreas; Arthur Conmy

record.tranche_reason: Tests linear representations and sparse dictionary features in a vision-language model, extending the question to image and multimodal representations rather than reproducing the toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstructions and evaluations, interpretability judgments, sparse approximations of steering vectors, and image-token steering. Values appearing only in figures are recorded as figure only. The SAE training settings and hyperparameters are not results. The image-token ablation results localize information transfer but do not directly test the listed claim versions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs and uses probes and steering in a vision-language model (LlaVA-Next 7b). Its results bear on whether SAEs recover sparse interpretable features (V4), how complete SAE dictionaries are (V5), and whether concepts are 1-D directions (V6). It does not reproduce the toy-model setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors find neurons form a highly interpretable basis over image information, comparing favorably to SAE features, unlike in LLMs. Add also that linear/SAE representations give an unnatural basis for adversarial attacks, and that text-derived vectors fail to steer image tokens.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear probes, contrastive activation addition, SAE training and sparse dictionary approximation in a vision-language model; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or test their sparsity-dependent superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering effectiveness varied by layer, with earlier layers more effective. SAE VQA performance depended on whether reconstructions were spliced into image tokens or all token positions.

fits_no_version.finding: The share of SAE features and neurons rated multimodal rises in deeper layers. Text-derived steering vectors (logit lens, text embeddings) steered image tokens no better than random vectors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VLLM representations of image and text are largely disjoint early and become more shared across modalities in deeper layers.

record.problems: The study focuses on one VLLM architecture and calls for evaluation across diverse architectures. Several reported results are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. The interpretability evaluation samples 25 SAE features and 50 neurons from each of five layers. The all-token SAE splice performs near chance on the reported VQA benchmarks.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, sparsity transition or geometry.
All of it: no test of whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
All of it: no test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Text-only LLMs, and direct measures of feature spread across neurons.
Stability across SAE runs or seeds, canonicality, and comparison across dictionary sizes.
Any comparison against multi-dimensional features, and whether the 1-D directions are superposed.

missing.what: Neurons form a worse dictionary than SAE features for sparsely approximating steering vectors. This compares the SAE and neuron bases, which bears on V4.
Features selected by the sparse approximation correspond to the positive and negative classes, with predictable activations on those images.
The Discussion states neurons form a highly interpretable basis over image information, unlike in language models, comparing favorably to SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's V6 limits_scope label based on layer dependence. The authors tie that dependence to where image information is transferred into text tokens (ablation after layer 12 is negligible), not to failure of the 1-D directions. Most quantitative values appear only in figures. The study is a single-model preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity alone indicates superposition.
The study tests SAE-recoverable features in one VLLM; it does not test feature spread across neurons in LLMs generally.
Tests reconstruction, interpretability and some feature approximation, but not feature stability across training runs or whether SAE features are canonical units.
Tests linear probes and causal steering vectors for image concepts, but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional feature representations or establish superposition.

rows.subject: LlaVA-Next 7b
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on end-to-end multimodal instruction following
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE-feature activation differences between original and adversarially attacked images

conditions.value: PGD adversarial attack using a single prompt

rows.measure: Sparsity and semantic alignment of activation differences in the SAE basis
rows.value: differences were usually dense, involved hundreds of SAE features, and the largest-changing features appeared random and did not directly correspond to the attack change
rows.note: The authors also report that attacks were brittle across prompts; this result concerns adversarial changes, not the completeness of ordinary model representations generally.
rows.check: The authors hoped the SAE basis would explain the adversarial changes. Instead the activation differences were dense, spanning hundreds of features, and the top features 'appeared to be random'. No sparse SAE account was found in this setting, so the state is absent, not partial.

source_check.correct: state: cannot_determine for V5. Adversarial activation differences involve hundreds of SAE features, with the largest changes lacking direct semantic correspondence to the attack; dictionary completeness is not measured.
source_check.problem: Dense, semantically unaligned changes do not demonstrate absent dictionary completeness.

rows.subject: LlaVA-Next 7b
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on end-to-end multimodal instruction following
rows.operation_detail: Added contrastive activation addition steering vectors at image-token positions

conditions.value: 50 randomly selected ImageNet class pairs in the main description

rows.measure: Steering score and coherence of generated captions
rows.value: targeted interventions steered outputs predictably; earlier-layer steering was more effective, with impact decreasing in deeper layers
rows.note: Appendix A separately describes an evaluation using 200 random ImageNet-class pairs.
rows.check: Steering along 1-D CAA directions worked predictably. The decline in deeper layers is explained by image-token ablation: image information has already moved to text tokens. It does not weaken the directional effect at the layers where image information is used.

rows.subject: LlaVA-Next 7b
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on end-to-end multimodal instruction following
rows.operation_detail: Trained linear probes on mean residual-stream embeddings across image-token positions
rows.baseline: modern self-supervised and supervised image classifiers
rows.value: figure only; linear probes achieved strong performance, on par with classifiers trained directly on self-supervised image representations
rows.note: The paper describes linear decodability, but this probe result alone does not show that the model causally uses the probed representation.

source_check.correct: state: cannot_determine for V6. Strong multiclass linear decodability does not distinguish one-dimensional features from multidimensional representations.
source_check.problem: A linear-probe result does not establish partially one-dimensional intrinsic feature structure.

relationships.condition: SAEs trained on residual streams of LlaVA-Next 7b, layers 8–24
relationships.reason: SAE features were judged interpretable (R6). ImageNet-class steering vectors were sparse in the SAE basis: under 100 features, and 20 features steered comparably to the dense vector (R9, R10).
relationships.display_finding: SAE features were judged interpretable, and ImageNet-class steering vectors used under 100 SAE features, with 20 features steering about as well as the dense vector.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: SAEs trained on residual streams of LlaVA-Next 7b, layers 8–24
source_check.reason: R6, R9 and R10 demonstrate interpretable dictionary features and sparse approximations of class directions in this setting.

relationships.condition: Neuron basis for image information in LlaVA-Next
relationships.reason: SAE features were only slightly more interpretable than neurons, and both were highly interpretable (R6). The authors say that, unlike in LLMs, neurons form a highly interpretable basis here. So the evidence for features spread across neurons is weak in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: SAE features were only slightly more interpretable than neurons, and both were highly interpretable. The authors note that, unlike in LLMs, neurons form a highly interpretable basis for image information here.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Neuron basis for image information in LlaVA-Next
source_check.reason: Interpretable neurons and a small SAE advantage do not establish absent distributed representations or failed sparse dictionary recovery. V4 does not require neurons to be uninterpretable.

relationships.reason: Splicing the SAE into image tokens caused only a slight VQA drop (R4). Class steering vectors were sparsely and faithfully represented in the SAE dictionary (R9, R10).
relationships.display_finding: The SAE splice caused only a slight VQA drop, and class steering vectors were sparsely and faithfully represented in the dictionary.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R4 reports a slight accuracy decrease, qualifying completeness even at image tokens. R9–R10 establish preservation of selected class directions; stability and canonicality remain untested.

relationships.condition: All-token splicing, adversarial perturbations, and loss recovered
relationships.reason: All-token splicing dropped VQA to near chance (R5). Adversarial activation changes were dense and not explained by SAE features (R11). Loss recovered is described only as fairly competitive (R1–R3).
relationships.display_finding: Substituting SAE reconstructions at every token dropped VQA to near chance, adversarial activation changes were dense and not explained by SAE features, and loss recovered was described only as fairly competitive.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: All-token splicing, adversarial perturbations, and loss recovered
source_check.reason: Split this condition group: R5 challenges behavioral completeness through near-chance VQA and incoherent responses after all-token substitution. R11 does not test completeness, and the qualitative loss descriptions in R1–R3 do not establish its degree.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-class concepts at image tokens, early-to-mid layers
relationships.reason: Single CAA direction vectors steered captions predictably toward target classes (R12). Linear probes decoded class strongly (R13), though the probe result alone is not causal.
relationships.display_finding: Single CAA direction vectors steered captions predictably toward target classes, and linear probes decoded class strongly, though the probe result alone is not causal.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: ImageNet-class concepts at image tokens, early-to-mid layers
source_check.reason: R12 supports causally effective one-dimensional class directions in this setting. R13 supplies decodability evidence only; neither result excludes multidimensional representations.
